stem: Meena is helping her grandmother clean up the kitchen after some things got mixed together. Each method of separation uses only one difference in properties. Which mixture needs a sequence of more than one separation method to separate it completely?

options.text: Iron nails mixed with sawdust, which can be separated with a magnet.
Sand, common salt and water mixed together, which must be separated step by step.
Pebbles mixed with water, which can be separated by filtering.
Salt dissolved in water, which can be separated by evaporation.

teacher.key_rationale: Options A, C and D each involve two components differing in one property (magnetism, particle size, solubility vs volatility), so a single method suffices. Option B contains three components, so no single property difference separates all of them at once; filtration removes the sand and evaporation then recovers the salt, so a sequence of methods is required.
